q: How much of the paper's 12 at% Cr diffusivity recovery magnitude (factor ~3× above the 5% minimum) is attributable to full per-edge NEB barriers versus finite-simulation-box effects? The paper's own Fig 14 shows 20-uc boxes give sub-linear MSD at 10 at% Cr — is the 80-uc paper box actually converged for the recovery, or is 1.67e-5 cm^2/s still biased by the largest channel spanning L (paper Fig 13(b))?
basis: Our coarse-grained per-shell KMC on a 20-uc box captured the drop-and-turnover trend qualitatively but under-reproduces the paper's steep recovery from 8.63e-6 (5% Cr) to 1.67e-5 (12% Cr), delivering only 8.76e-6 at 12%. Which of the two documented reductions (per-shell vs per-edge barriers; L=20 vs L=80) dominates the discrepancy is not disentangled here.
next_steps: Run the same coarse KMC at L=40 and L=80 uc for c_Cr=10-12% to isolate the finite-size effect. Separately, extend the per-shell rate model to a per-shell + per-transition-direction catalog matching all 12 barriers in paper Table II. Compare deltas.

q: Does the 1NN-basin percolation transition follow a power-law scaling of D at the critical c_Cr* consistent with 3D bond-percolation universality (beta ~ 0.41, nu ~ 0.88)? Our channel_cell_frac data (0.3% at 1% Cr, 5.6% at 5%, 23% at 12%) shows monotonic growth but we have not tested finite-size scaling.
basis: The paper attributes the recovery to a 'formation of interconnected channels' and quantifies channel count/size (Fig 13) but does not perform the finite-size-scaling analysis that would distinguish a percolation phase transition from a smooth crossover.
next_steps: Run KMC + channel-fraction analysis at L=10,15,20,30,40 for a dense c_Cr grid around the suspected c_Cr*. Fit D(c_Cr, L) ~ |c-c*|^(t-beta) * f(L^(1/nu)*|c-c*|) to extract exponents and compare with 3D percolation theory.

q: The paper assumes ferromagnetic Ni-Cr for all DFT below 12 at% Cr, and Table IV shows strongly repulsive Cr-Cr SRO at 12%. Does the effective percolation threshold c_Cr* shift when Cr atoms are dispersed by SRO instead of being randomly placed, and by how much?
basis: Repulsive Cr-Cr SRO physically inhibits Cr clustering, which is exactly what feeds the 1NN-basin percolation. The paper reports SRO suppresses D at 12% Cr but shows only two data points (5% and 12%) in Sec 3.5. The systematic c_Cr* shift is not quantified.
next_steps: Combine an MC-generated SRO configuration (using the paper's MDMC/Howells-Mishin potential) with our KMC across 0-12 at% Cr. Compare channel_cell_frac vs c_Cr with and without SRO. Report the effective c_Cr* shift.

q: The paper uses only static (T=0) DFT barriers and no vacancies. In reactor-relevant conditions, ballistic vacancy production is concurrent with He generation and Ni vacancies bind He very strongly (paper introduction: 'much higher effective barrier under vacancy-rich conditions'). How does adding a dilute vacancy population (say 100 ppm) modify the non-monotonic D(c_Cr) trend?
basis: The paper's conclusion pointing at 'extended defects such as dislocations are expected to significantly influence He diffusion and the formation of diffusion channels' but leaves this out of scope. Reactor-relevant answers about HTHE kinetics require this comparison.
next_steps: Extend the KMC with two additional site types (He-in-Ni-vacancy, He-near-vacancy) with binding/exit barriers from DFT literature (e.g. Ref [16] Adams & Wolfer 1988). Run 0-12 at% Cr with 100 ppm vacancies. Report D and channel_cell_frac shifts, and whether the recovery survives.

q: The paper's 3NN-T site has the deepest IFE (4.42 eV) yet remains an isolated trap because 3NN-T sites of different Cr atoms don't share low-barrier <110> connections. Is this a general FCC geometric statement, or Cr-specific? For Mo or W substitutions in Ni (Ref [13]), does the 1NN-basin also percolate the same way, or do trapping topologies differ enough that the non-monotonic recovery disappears entirely?
basis: The paper's Ref [13] (Ding et al. 2022) studied Cr, Mo, W in Ni and found different IFE landscapes. If 1NN-basin topology is Cr-specific, adding Mo or W will not exhibit the non-monotonic recovery even at high concentrations, which would be an actionable alloy-design insight for radiation-tolerant materials.
next_steps: Repeat this exact KMC pipeline with Ding et al.'s Mo and W IFE + barrier tables (published in JNM 565, 153720, 2022). Determine whether channel_cell_frac still grows and whether D turns over. Publish a short comparative note.
